faqs.question: Is a digital proposal card for a girlfriend actually free?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends which of five models the tool uses. Free can cover the editor only, the export with a watermark, a trial window, building and sending but not keeping, or genuinely the whole build-and-send. Find the export button before you design anything and you will know which one you are on.

faqs.question: What is usually the catch with a free proposal card maker?
faqs.answer: The commonest catch is that designing is free and downloading is not, so the paywall appears after you have done the work. The second commonest is a watermark burned into the file she receives. Both are visible in under two minutes if you export one throwaway card first.

faqs.question: Should I spend money on a gift instead of sending a free card?
faqs.answer: Spending is not automatically the stronger signal. A four-study Psychology & Marketing paper from February 2024 found that large gift expenditures can make recipients suspicious of a giver's motives, and that expenditures of time and effort — and gifts that are experiences rather than objects — are less prone to that suspicion and are appreciated more. Only that paper's published abstract was readable to us.

faqs.question: Do I have to pay to remove the watermark?
faqs.answer: On tools that use the watermark model, yes — that is the entire business model. Check by exporting a test card before you write anything personal. Some tools watermark only the preview and release a clean file, so the preview alone is not proof.

faqs.question: Do I need an account or a credit card to start?
faqs.answer: Varies by tool, and a payment method demanded at signup is the clearest sign you are on a trial that will bill you later. On SubhSandesh you can build a page, publish it and send the link without entering a card. We cannot publish our exact tier limits today, because our pricing data is unverified.

faqs.question: Does she need to install anything to open it?
faqs.answer: No, if you send a hosted link — it opens in whatever browser is already on her phone. That matters, because 48.9% of views of shared SubhSandesh pages arrive on a phone (25,008 of 51,164 views, platform-wide). A downloaded image file needs nothing either.

faqs.question: How long does it take to make one?
faqs.answer: Longer than the tools claim. The median gap between first save and last edit on SubhSandesh is 6.3 hours, sampled on the /love-gf page with n=1,136, which means people return to it across a day rather than finishing in one sitting. Budget an evening, not ten minutes.

faqs.question: Why does this search keep returning bridesmaid cards?
faqs.answer: Because 'proposal card' also means asking a friend to be a bridesmaid, and that market is much larger in search. On 17 September 2026, four of the ten results for 'proposal card online free' were bridesmaid stationery, printed marriage-proposal cards or business proposal templates. Add 'for girlfriend' or 'link' to filter them out.

faqs.question: Is a free card good enough for an actual marriage proposal?
faqs.answer: It can be, if the effort is real and the moment is not. A free page that took you an evening carries more signal than a paid template you changed three words in. If you are in the same room, propose in person and use the page as the keepsake.

faqs.question: What happens to the card or the link after I send it?
faqs.answer: That is the question most tools answer badly. Some links expire, some pages are deleted after a set window, and on some the link only stays reachable if you keep paying. Ask before you build, because for a proposal the link is the thing she will reopen.

faqs.question: Should I pay if I can afford it?
faqs.answer: Pay early rather than late, if the tool turns out to charge at download or after a trial. Losing an hour of work at a paywall on the evening you planned to ask is a worse outcome than spending a couple of hundred rupees at the start.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Digital Proposal Card for a Girlfriend, Online and Free

A digital proposal card for a girlfriend, online and free, is a card you build in a browser and send as a link or a file — and in this category the word "free" does five different jobs, only one of which still costs nothing at the end. Two numbers from SubhSandesh's own database frame it: 92.9% of started pages are published and shared (4,204 of 4,524 pages created since 12 March 2026), and 40.0% of creators password-protect the page before sending it (1,809 of 4,524). Both are platform-wide across all 16 page types, not proposal pages specifically. Below: the five kinds of free, what to check before you spend an hour designing, and whether a free card reads as cheap.

## What a digital proposal card for a girlfriend actually is

A digital proposal card is a card made for one person in a browser and delivered over the internet instead of by hand. It comes in two shapes: a file you download and drop into a chat, or a hosted link that opens into a page on her phone.

Which shape to choose is the subject of our guide to the [virtual proposal card](https://subhsandesh.in/blog/virtual-proposal-card). This page is about the other half: the money.

It is worth knowing what this search is not. On 17 September 2026, page one for "proposal card online free" carried two bridesmaid-card sites, one printed-stationery marketplace and one business-card template shop — four of ten results answering a different question.

A bridesmaid card asks a friend to stand at a wedding; a business template prices a project. Neither is a card for a girlfriend.

## Five kinds of "free", and which one you are looking at

Every tool here leads with the word. These are the five models behind it, each set out the same way: what free covers, where the money appears, what stopping costs.

### 1. Free to design, pay to download

Free covers the editor. You pick a template, drop in her name and your photos, and arrange it exactly as you want. The money appears at export: the download button opens a checkout, a plan picker or a credit purchase. Stop there and you lose the whole design, because nothing leaves the site without that export.

### 2. Free, with a watermark

Free covers the editor and the export. The money appears as a logo, a URL strip or a corner badge burned into the image she receives. Stop there and you lose nothing practical — but the card carries a stranger's brand into the one moment you were trying to make private.

### 3. Free trial, then a subscription

Free covers a window, usually seven or fourteen days, and usually asks for a card up front. The money appears on a date you have to remember, at monthly pricing built for people who send cards weekly. Stop there and you lose access to the card the day the trial lapses.

### 4. Free to make, paid to keep

Free covers building and sending. The money appears later, attached to time: the link expires, the page is deleted after a set period, or keeping it reachable becomes a paid feature. Stop there and you keep the proposal but lose the keepsake — and this is the link she reopens.

### 5. Free to build and free to share

Free covers making the page, publishing it and sending the link, with no card required to finish any of those steps. Where money enters at all, it sits on extras, not on the send. Stop there and you lose nothing at the moment of sending.

## What to check before you spend an hour on a design

An hour is a conservative estimate. The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit on SubhSandesh is 6.3 hours, sampled on the "I love you" page (/love-gf, n=1,136) — people build these across a day, in more than one sitting.

Check the export button before you write a single word. Start a card, then go straight to the download or share control. If it opens a plan picker, you have identified the model in ninety seconds rather than after six paragraphs written to her.

Check whether the export carries a watermark, not just the preview. Some tools mark the preview and release a clean file; others do the reverse, and the only reliable test is exporting a throwaway card.

Check whether a payment method is required to begin — a card demanded at signup is the clearest signal of model three. Put the end date in your calendar before you start designing.

Check where the page lives afterwards. If you are sending a link, ask what happens to it in six months, and if the tool does not say anywhere, treat the silence as the answer.

India's consumer regulator polices the word itself. The Central Consumer Protection Authority's Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements were notified on 9 June 2022 and [announced by the Press Information Bureau the next day](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1832906); they define what counts as a "free claim advertisement" and carry penalties of up to ₹10 lakh, rising to ₹50 lakh for a repeat contravention.

## Will a free card feel cheap to her?

This is the real worry under the search, and research answers it better than instinct. Money spent is not the signal most people assume.

A four-study paper in Psychology & Marketing, [published 14 February 2024](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mar.21983), found that large gift expenditures can make recipients suspicious of a giver's motives, and that the suspicion undermines the appreciation the spending was meant to earn. The same paper reports that expenditures of time and effort, and gifts that are experiences rather than objects, are less prone to that suspicion and are appreciated more.

A card that took you an evening is therefore not a weaker version of one that took your money. It is the version less likely to be read as instrumental.

Zero prices do change behaviour, though, and not always flatteringly. A natural field experiment [published in Experimental Economics on 26 May 2026](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/experimental-economics/article/role-of-social-norms-in-zero-price-effects/62AF95538420785B6341938B196AB7E8) found that taking a large quantity of a free good is rated as less socially appropriate than taking the same quantity priced at one cent, and that zero pricing raised the share of people who took anything while lowering the average amount taken.

Zero can also backfire outright. A five-study paper in the Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, [published 14 February 2022 under CC BY](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11747-022-00842-1), describes a "boomerang effect" where a zero price lowers demand compared with a low price when the offer carries high incidental costs, because zero triggers scrutiny of those costs.

An earlier Psychology & Marketing study, [from 11 April 2019](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/mar.21211), names two intuitions people bring to a free digital offer: a "free mentality" expecting digital things to cost nothing, and a price–quality inference reading zero as a quality signal. Only the price–quality one works against you.

## What "free" covers on SubhSandesh, and what we cannot tell you

You can build a page, put your photos and your words on it, publish it and send the link without paying and without entering a card. That much we can state plainly.

What we will not print is a tier table. The pricing block in our own first-party data file is empty — not derivable from the database, and not filled in by hand — so we cannot tell you today where paying starts. Check the template page itself before you start, rather than trusting a number we cannot stand behind.

What we can measure is behaviour. 92.9% of started pages reach a recipient (4,204 of 4,524) and 40.0% of creators lock the page with a password first (1,809 of 4,524) — both platform-wide across 16 page types, neither proposal-specific.

## Which page to send her

"For my girlfriend" covers two different questions, and the page should match the one you are actually asking. The counts below are real, out of 4,524 pages.

| Page | The question it asks | Pages created | Share of all pages |
|---|---|---|---|
| Will You Marry Me? | Marriage, as a scrapbook ending in a YES button | not published separately | — |
| I love you page | "Will you be my girlfriend" or "I love you" | 1,136 | 25.1% |
| Apology dashboard | Sorry first, ask second | 1,095 | 24.2% |
| Build-a-Bouquet | Flowers instead of a question | 1,094 | 24.2% |
| Darling | A darker, more dramatic romantic page | 436 | 9.6% |

The blank row is deliberate: proposal-specific creation figures were not obtainable for this batch, and we will not derive one from a neighbouring template.

If the question is marriage, the [Will You Marry Me? proposal scrapbook](https://subhsandesh.in/proposal) is built for it. If "for my girlfriend" actually means "will you be my girlfriend", the [I love you page](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf) is the honest fit — at 1,136 pages it is the most-created thing here. If she would rather have flowers than a question, [Build-a-Bouquet](https://subhsandesh.in/bouquet-gf) hands her twelve blooms to arrange.

## When a free digital proposal card is the wrong choice

If you are in the same room, send nothing. A link solves distance; using one at arm's length turns a moment into an errand on her phone.

If she has said she wants something she can hold, a card on a screen is the wrong object however well made. Printed stationery and a ring box win, and the 48.9% of views that arrive on a phone (25,008 of 51,164) are beside the point for someone who wanted paper.

And if the tool you found is model one or model three, pay early. An hour lost at a paywall on the evening you planned to ask is worse than ₹200 spent at the start.

## Sources

- [Suspicion of large gift expenditures undermines gift appreciation](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mar.21983) — Psychology & Marketing, 14 February 2024
- [The role of social norms in zero price effects](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/experimental-economics/article/role-of-social-norms-in-zero-price-effects/62AF95538420785B6341938B196AB7E8) — Experimental Economics, online 26 May 2026, CC BY
- [The boomerang effect of zero pricing](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11747-022-00842-1) — Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 14 February 2022, CC BY
- [The zero-price effect in freemium business models](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/mar.21211) — Psychology & Marketing, 11 April 2019
- [Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements, 2022](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1832906) — Press Information Bureau, 10 June 2022

Three of these were read at abstract level only — both Psychology & Marketing papers and the JAMS one, whose publishers block automated fetchers. Nothing beyond the registered abstract is claimed above.

The three publisher pages — onlinelibrary.wiley.com x2 and link.springer.com — return HTTP 403 or a Cloudflare challenge to any automated fetcher, so each claim was verified against the publisher-registered abstract via the Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/<DOI>) rather than the landing page, and the body now states that in prose under ## Sources. auditReport.honestAssessment: REWRITTEN AFTER THE FIX PASS, 2026-09-17. An answer engine would cite this over the SERP incumbents because none of them is an article: on 17 September 2026 the top results were two marketplace listing grids, a JavaScript-only template search, three tool landing pages of 495-765 words and one competitor page of 1,645 words, and not one of them defines what its own "free" covers or cites a single number. This page names five free models, gives a ninety-second test for identifying which one a tool is running, and pairs that with peer-reviewed zero-price and gift-suspicion findings plus first-party behaviour data no competitor can publish. Ranking is a separate question and the post does not win it: subhsandesh.in has 46 live proposal pages and ranked in none of the 11 SERPs measured in the keyword run, so assume no authority on this query and do not expect the page to displace a tool landing page that already converts. The post's real weak point is unchanged by the fix pass, and it is the one a bottom-of-funnel reader actually arrives with: SubhSandesh's own free limits are NOT verifiable, because the Pricing block in content/facts.md is empty and has never been filled in by hand. The post states only that a page can be built, published and shared without entering a card, and refuses to print a tier table. The refusal is the honest move and it is also a worse reader experience than a table would be; closing it needs the pricing facts entered by hand, not more writing. Second gap, also unchanged: no proposal-specific figures exist for this batch, because the read-only probe of the proposalpages collection was blocked by production-read policy. Every SubhSandesh number here is therefore labelled in body prose as platform-wide across 16 page types (40.0% password-protected, 92.9% published and shared, 48.9% phone views, out of 4,524 pages) or as sampled on /love-gf (6.3-hour median edit gap, n=1,136), and the comparison table leaves the /proposal row's count blank on purpose. What the fix pass closed: the abstract-only disclosure now appears in the body under ## Sources instead of living only in this audit; the two brand names used as SERP examples were replaced with descriptions, since both sell into the same buyer; one FAQ that restated an H2 was replaced with a question the body does not answer. What it could not close: three of the five cited pages (onlinelibrary.wiley.com x2, link.springer.com) return 403 or a bot challenge to any automated fetcher, so those claims rest on Crossref-registered abstracts and nothing beyond them was read; and the upward link to the parent post /blog/virtual-proposal-card is a blog URL rather than a TEMPLATE_LINKS entry, so it 404s until that sibling publishes in the same batch.
